_note: Follow-up to eu-government-finance-2026-08-28.json, which left PT, RO, SI and CY's `*-edp-inventory` nodes wired only to eu-reg-479-2009 and esa-2010, with no national data end. Each country's NSI had already failed or come up empty in that round; this round retried each one via its FINANCE MINISTRY (or, where the lead said otherwise, a different domain/path on the same NSI). LANDED FOR ALL FOUR: PT (Banco de Portugal, not the Ministry of Finance -- dgo.gov.pt loaded via curl with -k, a real SSL cert-CN mismatch rather than a block, but is a JS-rendered SharePoint shell with no server-rendered body text, so it was not used as evidence; bportugal.pt's own domain 403'd WebFetch and curl alike, but its bpstat.bportugal.pt subdomain and api/media file endpoint both loaded cleanly), RO (Ministerul Finanțelor's own /static/ PDF endpoint -- non-static mfinante.gov.ro pages failed a robots.txt fetch, but the static PDF host did not), SI (not the finance ministry after all -- SURS/stat.si's own document endpoint at a THIRD path, after two paths were previously ROBOTS_DISALLOWED, per the specific lead to keep trying stat.si paths -- but the document names the Ministry of Finance, Ministrstvo za finance, as the preparer of the underlying public-finance balances), CY (found via the gov.cy government portal rather than mof.gov.cy directly, but the release's own contact address is at cystat.mof.gov.cy -- CYSTAT operating on a Ministry-of-Finance subdomain -- which is the concrete link the task's lead was gesturing at; mof.gov.cy's own public-debt page loaded but only cited CyStat as its source rather than stating methodology itself, so it was not used). 4 nodes, 10 edges (PT and RO did not get a Eurostat-transmission edge -- see _dropped). No eu-reg-479-2009 edge was minted for PT or CY (their fetched pages named other EU regulations, not 479/2009 by number); RO named no EU regulation number at all; SI is the strongest of the four, naming Reg 479/2009 by number, by CELEX number, and by article.

reports.title: Procedimento de Défices Excessivos — Notificação (Dívida e Défice das Administrações Públicas)
reports.publisher: Banco de Portugal, Departamento de Estatística
reports.description: Banco de Portugal's twice-yearly Excessive Deficit Procedure statistical note, updating Portugal's general government debt and deficit statistics alongside each EDP notification. The most recent edition states "O Banco de Portugal publica hoje as estatísticas da dívida pública anual atualizadas com a primeira notificação do Procedimento dos Défices Excessivos (PDE) de 2026 e uma análise da dívida pública portuguesa entre 2000 e 2025" (Banco de Portugal today publishes the annual public debt statistics updated with the first notification of the Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP) of 2026, and an analysis of Portuguese public debt between 2000 and 2025). ine.pt (Portugal's NSI) failed on three prior attempts across earlier rounds; this round went to Banco de Portugal instead, per the task lead, and it loaded cleanly.
reports.cadence_note: Twice yearly, on the EDP notification cycle -- editions found dated for the 1st notification of 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 (April) and the 2nd notification of 2023, 2024 and 2025 (October/November).

reports.title: Raport privind datoria publică guvernamentală — Report on Government Public Debt
reports.publisher: Ministerul Finanţelor (Ministry of Finance, Romania), Direcția Generală de Trezorerie și Datorie Publică
reports.description: Romania's Ministry of Finance annual report on government public debt, which also reports the general government deficit under EU methodology alongside the cash-basis figure the Ministry itself compiles. The 31 December 2023 edition states: "Deficitul bugetului general consolidat în termeni cash, în anul 2023 a fost de 5,68% din PIB, în timp ce deficitul bugetar calculat conform metodologiei UE (ESA 2010) a reprezentat 6,6% din PIB" (The consolidated general budget deficit in cash terms in 2023 was 5.68% of GDP, while the budget deficit calculated according to EU methodology (ESA 2010) represented 6.6% of GDP). insse.ro (Romania's NSI) failed with a robots.txt block in the prior round; this round went to the Ministry of Finance instead, per the task lead.
reports.cadence_note: Dated editions found monthly (e.g. "Raportdatoriapub022025.pdf") alongside an annual year-end edition; releases_per_year reflects the monthly series rather than the annual one this node's evidence was drawn from.

reports.title: Primanjkljaj in dolg države — Metodološko pojasnilo (Deficit and Debt of the State — Methodological Note)
reports.publisher: Statistični urad Republike Slovenije (SURS) / Statistical Office of the Republic of Slovenia
reports.description: SURS's methodological note for its "Poročilo o presežnem primanjkljaju in dolgu, Slovenija, letno" (Report on excessive deficit and debt, Slovenia, annual) release. It names its legal basis outright: "Uredba (EU) Evropskega parlamenta in Sveta št. 549/2013 o Evropskem sistemu nacionalnih in regionalnih računov v Evropski uniji (CELEX 32013R0549)" and "Uredba Sveta (ES) št. 479/2009 o uporabi Protokola o postopku v zvezi s čezmernim primanjkljajem, ki je priloga k Pogodbi o ustanovitvi Evropske skupnosti (CELEX 32009R0479)" (Council Regulation (EC) No. 479/2009 on the application of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure, annexed to the Treaty establishing the European Community). It also names its main data source: "Bilance javnega financiranja pripravlja Ministrstvo za finance" (The public-finance balances are prepared by the Ministry of Finance) -- Slovenia's Ministry of Finance feeds this SURS release, which is the concrete finance-ministry link this round's lead pointed at, even though SURS remains the publisher of record. stat.si had returned ROBOTS_DISALLOWED on two other document paths in the prior round; this specific document path loaded cleanly via a direct fetch, per the task's instruction to keep trying stat.si paths rather than abandoning the domain.
reports.cadence_note: The document states it directly: "SURS pošilja Eurostatu tabele EDP, v celoti izpolnjene z zahtevanimi podatki, dvakrat letno: v okviru aprilske (pred prvim aprilom) in oktobrske (pred prvim oktobrom) notifikacije EDP" (SURS sends Eurostat the EDP tables, fully completed with the required data, twice a year: within the April (before 1 April) and October (before 1 October) EDP notification).

reports.title: Excessive Deficit Procedure and Annual Accounts of General Government
reports.publisher: Statistical Service of Cyprus (CYSTAT) -- operating on the Ministry of Finance's domain (contact address cystat.mof.gov.cy), published via the gov.cy government portal
reports.description: CYSTAT's annual EDP fiscal-results press release, republished on the gov.cy whole-of-government portal. It states "The Statistical Service announces the preliminary fiscal results for 2025, which have been audited and verified within the Excessive Deficit Procedure framework of the European Commission," and, on methodology, "The categories of revenue and expenditure for General Government cover all the subsectors of the General Government based on the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)" and "For the completion of the estimates, any methodological adjustments or corrections based on the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010) are taken into account." The document's own contact line names an email at cystat.mof.gov.cy, a subdomain of the Ministry of Finance's mof.gov.cy -- CyStat's own homepage (cystat.gov.cy) had shown no government-finance content in the prior round, and mof.gov.cy's own public-debt page (fetched again this round) only cites CyStat as an external source rather than stating methodology itself, so this gov.cy release -- reached via the Ministry-of-Finance-hosted CyStat address the task's lead pointed toward -- was used instead.
reports.cadence_note: INFERRED from the existence of both a 2024 and a 2025 dated edition of the same title on gov.cy, matching the standard EU April/October EDP cycle; no sentence on the fetched page states the cadence outright.

dependencies.basis: Banco de Portugal's EDP statistical note states "O Banco de Portugal publica hoje as estatísticas da dívida pública anual atualizadas com a primeira notificação do Procedimento dos Défices Excessivos (PDE) de 2026" (Banco de Portugal today publishes the annual public debt statistics updated with the first notification of the Excessive Deficit Procedure of 2026) -- this is the national EDP deficit/debt data whose methods and sources Portugal's Article 9 inventory documents.

Banco de Portugal's own methodological document for this release states "os conceitos subjacentes à compilação das estatísticas das finanças públicas estão incluídos no manual do Sistema Europeu de Contas Nacionais e Regionais – SEC" (the concepts underlying the compilation of public finance statistics are contained in the manual of the European System of National and Regional Accounts -- SEC, Portugal's name for ESA), citing "Regulamento (UE) n.º 549/2013 do Parlamento Europeu e do Conselho, de 21 de maio de 2013, sobre Sistema Europeu de Contas Nacionais e Regionais" -- the ESA 2010 regulation by number.

The release is explicitly framed as the statistical note accompanying Portugal's own EDP notification -- "a primeira notificação do Procedimento dos Défices Excessivos (PDE) de 2026" (the first notification of the Excessive Deficit Procedure of 2026) -- the national submission behind Eurostat's EDP notification tables.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Nos termos dos Regulamentos da União Europeia, Portugal disponibiliza ao Eurostat, até ao final de março, a primeira notificação do procedimento dos défices excessivos (PDE).

"Deficitul bugetului general consolidat în termeni cash, în anul 2023 a fost de 5,68% din PIB, în timp ce deficitul bugetar calculat conform metodologiei UE (ESA 2010) a reprezentat 6,6% din PIB" -- the report's own text ties its EU-methodology deficit figure to ESA 2010 by name.

The fetched report names only domestic Romanian instruments (OUG nr. 146/2002, OUG nr. 64/2007) and ESA 2010 by name -- no sentence names Regulation 479/2009 specifically, so the edge was not minted.

Banco de Portugal's methodological document names "Regulamento (UE) n.º 220/2014 da Comissão de 7 de março de 2014, que altera o Regulamento (CE) n.º 479/2009 do Conselho" (Commission Regulation (EU) No 220/2014, which AMENDS Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009) -- a real citation, but of the amending instrument rather than 479/2009 itself, and this session judged that one step removed from the direct citation this project's other eu-reg-479-2009 edges carry. Worth revisiting: a case could be made either way.

The fetched gov.cy release names ESA 2010 twice but no EU regulation by number for the EDP mechanism itself -- only "the Excessive Deficit Procedure framework of the European Commission" in prose. No 479/2009 citation found.

_dropped.edge: www.dgo.gov.pt (Direção-Geral do Orçamento, Portuguese Ministry of Finance)
_dropped.why: TECHNICAL NOTE, not a content failure. www.dgo.gov.pt returned a real HTTP 200 via curl with -k (its TLS certificate has an unrelated hostname in the Common Name -- issued to *.eo.gov.pt -- which is why both WebFetch and a verifying curl refused it; this reads as a shared-hosting cert misconfiguration on the Portuguese government's side, not a deliberate block). But the page itself is a SharePoint site (dgo.gov.pt/EstatisticasFinancasPublicas/Paginas/Procedimento-dos-Defices-Excessivos.aspx) that renders its content client-side via JavaScript; the raw HTML fetched is entirely _layouts/15 script-registration boilerplate with no server-rendered body text. Not used as evidence for that reason -- Banco de Portugal was used instead, and it is the actual publisher of Portugal's EDP statistical notes regardless. A browser-rendered fetch (Claude in Chrome) of the DGO page is the obvious next step if a second Portuguese source is wanted.
_dropped.note: dgo.gov.pt is otherwise reachable (HTTP 200), just not server-rendered.

_dropped.why: Loaded successfully and shows real Cypriot public-debt figures ("fiscal debt of €23,036.4 mn, which corresponds to 77.3% of GDP" for 2023), but the page's own text attributes the data to CyStat as an external source rather than stating ESA 2010 or EDP methodology on its own account -- it is a dashboard of headline numbers, not a methodology-bearing release. The gov.cy / cystat.mof.gov.cy release was used instead because it actually states its own methodology.
